facts.text: The order was made Wednesday, 17 March 2021 by Chief Justice Morawetz.
facts.quote: THE HONOURABLE CHIEF JUSTICE MORAWETZ ) WEDNESDAY, THE 17th DAY OF MARCH, 2021

facts.text: The motion was brought by LU under the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (CCAA).
facts.quote: THIS MOTION, brought by Laurentian University of Sudbury ("LU") pursuant to the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-36, as amended

facts.text: The motion was heard by videoconference via Zoom in Toronto because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
facts.quote: was heard this day by videoconference via Zoom in Toronto, Ontario due to the COVID-19 pandemic

facts.text: The Transfer Ratio is set at 65.8%.
facts.quote: shall be permitted to transfer commuted values from the Pension Plan based on a transfer ratio equal to 65.8% (the "Transfer Ratio")

facts.text: The 65.8% ratio comes from the most recently filed actuarial valuation report, effective 1 January 2020 and filed with FSRA in December 2020.
facts.quote: being the transfer ratio contained in the most recently filed actuarial valuation report for the Pension Plan (effective as of January 1, 2020 and filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020)

facts.text: Interim CV Applicants are those who received a retirement/termination statement and election form indicating they may elect a 100% commuted value transfer, and for whom the transfer has not yet been made.
facts.quote: for any individual who has received a retirement or termination statement and election form from LU indicating that he or she may elect to receive a 100% commuted value transfer from the Pension Plan and for whom such transfers have not yet been made (the "Interim CV Applicants")

facts.text: Interim CV Applicants get a re-election form and must elect in writing within 30 days of notice of the order.
facts.quote: shall be given a re-election form, which form must be submitted in writing to LU within 30 days of notice of this Order

facts.text: An Interim CV Applicant who does not elect within 30 days is DEEMED TO HAVE WITHDRAWN the transfer application and retains only a deferred pension.
facts.quote: shall be deemed to have withdrawn their application for a transfer of their commuted value and shall retain their entitlement to a deferred pension from the Pension Plan

facts.text: The PBGF Assessment Payment is stayed and suspended.
facts.quote: is stayed and suspended in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order of this Court dated February 11, 2021

facts.text: There is a SECOND, separate Incremental PBGF Assessment Payment covering the earlier pre-filing period 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019, triggered by the December 2020 filing of a new actuarial valuation. It is also stayed. Its amount is NOT stated in the document.
facts.quote: any incremental amount owing by LU in respect of its pro rata portion of assessment fees payable to the Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund relating to the Pension Plan for the pre-filing period of July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019 due to the filing in December 2020 of a new actuarial valuation report

facts.text: The stay flows from paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order dated 11 February 2021.
facts.quote: in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order of this Court dated February 11, 2021

facts.text: No LU director, officer, employee, agent, advisor or consultant incurs any obligation or liability as a result of the stay.
facts.quote: none of LU or any of its directors, officers, employees, agents, advisors or consultants shall incur any obligation or liability as a result of the stay and suspension

facts.text: Despite the stay, FSRA is expressly NOT precluded from asserting a claim against LU for either PBGF payment.
facts.quote: nothing in this Order shall preclude the Financial Services Regulatory Authority from asserting a claim against LU in respect of the PBGF Assessment Payment or the Incremental PBGF Assessment Payment

facts.text: Future adjustments to the Transfer Ratio are to be made under the Pension Benefits Act (PBA) or by further order of the court.
facts.quote: any future adjustments to the applicable Transfer Ratio for the purpose of commuted value transfers shall be established in accordance with the PBA, or by further Order of this Court

facts.text: The court requests the aid and recognition of any court, tribunal, regulatory or administrative body in Canada or the United States.
facts.quote: THIS COURT HEREBY REQUESTS the aid and recognition of any court, tribunal, regulatory or administrative body, having jurisdiction in Canada or in the United States of America

facts.text: Five Interim CV Applicants appeared: Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley and Sheila McGillis. No one appeared for the remaining Interim CV Applicants.
facts.quote: the following Interim CV Applicants, Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley and Sheila McGillis, with no one appearing for any other person on the service list or the remaining Interim CV Applicants

facts.text: The court read: the Notice of Motion dated 8 March 2021; the Initial Haché Affidavit sworn 30 January 2021; the Affidavit of Bobbie-Jo Brinkman sworn 8 March 2021; and the Second Report of the Monitor dated 11 March 2021.
facts.quote: ON READING the Notice of Motion of LU dated March 8, 2021, the affidavit of Dr. Robert Haché sworn January 30, 2021 and the Exhibits thereto (the "Initial Haché Affidavit") … the Affidavit of Bobbie-Jo Brinkman sworn March 8, 2021 and the Exhibits thereto and the Second Report of the Monitor dated March 11, 2021

facts.text: LU is both sponsor AND administrator of the Pension Plan.
facts.quote: LU, in its capacity as an Applicant herein and as sponsor and administrator of the Pension Plan

must_not_miss.text: The signature block: CHIEF JUSTICE G.B. MORAWETZ.
must_not_miss.why: Page 4 is a 252-character orphan page. Easy to skip entirely.

must_not_miss.text: The Incremental PBGF Assessment Payment — a second stayed payment, amount not stated.
must_not_miss.why: Sits behind the $842,018.34 in the same sentence. Extractions reliably capture the number and drop the unquantified second payment.

must_not_miss.text: The FSRA carve-out: the stay does not preclude FSRA from asserting a claim.
must_not_miss.why: Reverses the paragraph it sits in. Dropping it inverts the meaning of the order.

must_not_miss.text: The 30-day deemed-withdrawal rule: an Interim CV Applicant who does not re-elect in writing loses the commuted value transfer and keeps only a deferred pension.
must_not_miss.why: The consequence clause runs across a page break — precisely where section-chunked extraction loses text.

must_not_miss.text: Derek Harland appears in two capacities: deponent of the Affidavit of Service (p. 2) and counsel at TGF (p. 5).
must_not_miss.why: Requires joining the front and back of the document. A per-section extractor sees the two mentions in different chunks and will usually emit two unlinked entities, or one.

must_not_miss.text: The five named Interim CV Applicants (Leduc, Zapalski, Pegoraro, Oxley, McGillis) — real pensioners, named in the recital.
must_not_miss.why: Buried in a long procedural sentence about service. These are the human beings the 65.8% ratio is being applied to; an extractor tuned to institutions will drop them.

X.summary: This is a March 17, 2021 Ontario Superior Court of Justice Commercial List order governing pension issues in Laurentian University of Sudbury's CCAA proceeding. The court authorized 65.8% commuted-value pension transfers for eligible interim applicants, required affected applicants to re-elect within 30 days, and provided that nonresponders would retain deferred-pension entitlements. It also stayed Laurentian's $842,018.34 Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payment due March 30, 2021, as well as a potential incremental assessment, while preserving the regulator's ability to assert a claim. The order identifies five Interim CV Applicants who appeared and lists Thornton Grout Finnigan LLP as Laurentian's counsel.

key_facts.fact: The Ontario Superior Court of Justice Commercial List issued a pension order in Laurentian University of Sudbury's CCAA proceeding, court file CV-21-00656040-00CL.
Laurentian University of Sudbury is the sponsor and administrator of the Pension Plan.

The court authorized Laurentian University of Sudbury to transfer commuted values from the Pension Plan using a 65.8% transfer ratio for eligible Interim CV Applicants whose transfers had not yet been made.

The 65.8% transfer ratio was taken from the Pension Plan's most recently filed actuarial valuation report, effective January 1, 2020 and filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020.

Interim CV Applicants who had elected a commuted value transfer were required to re-elect within 30 days of receiving notice of the order between an immediate or deferred pension, as applicable, and a commuted value transfer based on the 65.8% transfer ratio.
An Interim CV Applicant who failed to make a written election within the 30-day period would be deemed to have withdrawn the transfer application and would retain entitlement to a deferred pension.

The court stayed and suspended Laurentian University of Sudbury's $842,018.34 payment due March 30, 2021 for its pro rata share of Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment fees for the July 1, 2019–June 30, 2020 pre-filing period, together with related interest and penalties.

The stay also covered any incremental amount owed for the July 1, 2018–June 30, 2019 assessment period resulting from the Pension Plan's new actuarial valuation report filed in December 2020, together with related interest and penalties.

The order did not prevent the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario from asserting a claim against Laurentian University of Sudbury for the stayed Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment amounts.
The pension-payment stay was stated to operate under paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order dated February 11, 2021.

Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley and Sheila McGillis appeared as Interim CV Applicants at the hearing; no one appeared for the other persons on the service list or the remaining Interim CV Applicants.
Thornton Grout Finnigan LLP acted as counsel for Laurentian University of Sudbury in the application.

Z.summary: This is a March 17, 2021 Pension Order of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice Commercial List in Laurentian University of Sudbury's CCAA proceeding, addressing commuted-value pension transfers and Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessments. The order authorizes eligible transfers at a 65.8% ratio, requires affected applicants to re-elect within 30 days or retain deferred pensions, and stays the $842,018.34 assessment due March 30, 2021 along with a possible incremental assessment. It preserves the regulator's ability to claim the stayed amounts and seeks assistance from Canadian and U.S. authorities.

key_facts.fact: On March 17, 2021, the Ontario Superior Court of Justice Commercial List heard and issued a pension order in Laurentian University of Sudbury's CCAA proceeding by videoconference in Toronto, Ontario.
The court file number for the Laurentian University of Sudbury CCAA proceeding is CV-21-00656040-00CL.

The court permitted Laurentian University of Sudbury, as sponsor and administrator of the Pension Plan, to transfer commuted values at a 65.8% transfer ratio for eligible Interim CV Applicants whose previously issued forms indicated they could elect a 100% transfer and whose transfers had not yet been made.

The 65.8% transfer ratio is the ratio in the Pension Plan's most recently filed actuarial valuation report, effective January 1, 2020 and filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020.

Interim CV Applicants who had elected a commuted value transfer must receive a re-election form from Laurentian University of Sudbury and submit a written election within 30 days after notice of the order, choosing an immediate or deferred pension or a commuted-value transfer at the 65.8% ratio.

An Interim CV Applicant who does not make the required written election within the 30-day period is deemed to have withdrawn the commuted-value transfer application and retains entitlement to a deferred Pension Plan pension.
Future adjustments to the transfer ratio must be made under the Ontario Pension Benefits Act and its regulations or by further order of the court.

The court stayed the $842,018.34 Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payment due March 30, 2021, covering Laurentian University of Sudbury's pro rata assessment fees for the Pension Plan's July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020 pre-filing period, together with applicable interest and penalties.

The stay also covers any incremental pro rata Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment for the July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019 pre-filing period arising from the new actuarial valuation report filed in December 2020, together with applicable interest and penalties.

The order provides that Laurentian University of Sudbury and its directors, officers, employees, agents, advisors and consultants incur no obligation or liability as a result of the stay, while preserving the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario's ability to assert a claim against Laurentian University of Sudbury for the stayed amounts.

Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley and Sheila McGillis appeared at the hearing as Interim CV Applicants; no one appeared for other persons on the service list or the remaining Interim CV Applicants, although the order states they were duly served.

The court requested that courts, tribunals and regulatory or administrative bodies in Canada and the United States of America recognize and assist Laurentian University of Sudbury and the Monitor in implementing the order, including granting the Monitor representative status in a foreign proceeding if necessary.
